summary: Camp Creek Bald Lookout, a steel tower built in 1928 or 1929 in Pisgah National Forest, got a round cab in the 1960s and is locked and no longer active.

facts.design: 14 x 14 ft observation cab on a steel tower, later fitted with one of two prototype round cabs (1960s)

access.note: Per the September 20, 2020 visit report, the cab trap door was locked to prevent access; per the September 20, 2008 visit report, the catwalk gate was locked and wrapped in razor wire

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Pisgah National Forest

events.note: Built with a 14 x 14 ft cab on a 21 ft steel tower, per the National Historic Lookout Register
One of two prototype round cabs installed in the 1960s; the exact year is not given
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register April 2, 2008, nominated by Peter J. Barr

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1928 and a 21-ft tower; Forest Lookouts gives 1929 and a 20-ft tower for the same 14 x 14 cab. Neither source explains the other, so both are noted in the story and the year is not settled.

notes_for_editor: DUPLICATE: this record is the same tower as us-nc-camp-creek-bald (NHLR US 719; tnlandforms NCT023 'Camp Creek Bald', 36.02333, -82.71555, GA 3398). That record already has a full story and research, and this story repeats its facts from the same register page. Recommend merging or hiding one record; this one has no independent sourcing beyond the NHLR page and the Forest Lookouts page. The 1928 vs 1929 and 21 ft vs 20 ft figures are unresolved. The poor-condition comments come from the September 20, 2020 visit report on the same NHLR page; the catwalk gate note and the 'very good shape' rating come from the September 20, 2008 report. Because both come from one register page, the visit-report claims are not independent sources.
